chapter: Caravan, Perdido and the first tunes
title: Irving Mills as title-giver and lyricist, not composer
summary: Tizol and Rose agree Mills named tunes and wrote lyrics but did not write the music he later claimed to have edited.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Uh huh. So Caravan was probably named by Irving Mills?
I know that Lawrence told me that Irving Mills named a lot of tunes.
Yeah, he was a lyric writer -- after he put the lyrics together he would put the name on it, whatever he thought was best.
Did Irving Mills ever have anything to do with the music part, I mean, with actually writing or arranging, or anything?
Listen, when it comes to that, I don't know. I don't know if Irving Mills wrote any music or not; I just don't know.
But things with you and Duke did that Irving Mills's name is on -- the ones where your names were on them -- he didn't write any of the music, did he?
No, no. I don't think so. No.
He didn't write the music -- Juan wrote the music.
Yes, I know, but he claims that he changed things around and he edited, and made a musical contribution, but I can't find anybody else who remembers him doing anything like that.
I don't think he remembers, either.
